children: has recorded its sharpest five-day selloff since the March 2020 COVID-19 crash and its second-largest decline on record, according to Global Macro Strategist at Vanda Research, Viraj Patel.
A chart showed the ETF's five-day rate of change at -14.02%. MTUM was last at $64.13, compared with its June 22, 2026, high of $86.31.

The decline comes as the momentum strategy faces an unusually sharp reversal. Porfolio manager, Blake Millard, cited J.P. Morgan's assessment that momentum experienced its second six-sigma unwinding day in roughly a week following major hyperscaler earnings reports last week.
The move deepened the strategy's decline and produced its largest single-month underperformance in more than 40 years, at 5.8 standard deviations, he said.

J.P. Morgan's data showed cap-weighted momentum underperformed the broader market by 10.8% in October, its largest single-month underperformance in the chart's history, which dates back to 1985. The chart also showed a 9.8% outperformance in April 2026 and underperformance of roughly 7% in 2008.

A separate J.P. Morgan chart tracking daily returns in cap-weighted momentum shows the Oct. 22, 2026, reading of -6.63 standard deviations as the largest marked negative-sigma episode in the chart window, which begins in 2023. The other marked episodes are -6.3 on Feb. 2, 2023, -6.03 on July 16, 2026, and -5.9 on Jan. 27, 2025.

title: Momentum ETF suffers biggest five-day selloff since COVID-19 crash
